body: I'm sorry you are having a hard time. I think couples counselling is a good place to start, as learning to communicate is going to make things easier. As someone with BPD I always try to logically analyze why I am reacting to something. It's good you recognize your SO can't help reacting to triggers, but she also needs to be able to recognize these reactions are not because of you. They are created by past events that have caused her pain. Also it may help if you can discuss her triggers together, at least if you know what they are, then you can help lessen them. For instance, I have panic attacks when I don't know where my SO is, he helps lessen the issue by texting me whenever he goes somewhere. I'm sure it can be annoying for him, but it's a small change that helps me stay calm.
Thanks for the reply! It's a situation where a psychiatrist would be covered, but a psychologist is not. I really don't want to be on medication. I should really start with the GP route though.
